messages:
Alice Nguyen: Quick follow-up from the FlashAttention integration RFC — saw some weird perf deltas in canary runs, posting data and questions.
Bob Chen: yep saw that in the dashboard, curious what shapes you tested.
Alice Nguyen: baseline = non-flash kernel (our old fused kernel). v3 flash gives ~25% win on long seqs (1k+), but at seq<=64 we see 10-15% regressions and latency p50 jitter. cpu-side queueing looks normal. :thinking:
Carlos Rivera: did you run with the same workspace config? v3 has different workspace allocation patterns.
Alice Nguyen: good call. I ran with default workspace pooling enabled. When I force flash v3 to use per-request allocation, regression goes away but memory spills increase. Not sure if pooling interaction is the culprit.
Dina Patel: can you paste the canary config and a small perf log?
Alice Nguyen: sure — snippet of the thing I used:
```
kernel.prefer = "flash_v3"
kernel.fallback = "flash_v2,legacy_fused"
workspace.pool = true
workspace.pool_size_gb = 6
heuristics.short_seq_threshold = 128
```
Log sample (p50/p95 in ms):
```
baseline (legacy_fused): p50=18.4 p95=34.9
flash_v3 (pool=true): p50=21.3 p95=48.1
flash_v3 (pool=false): p50=18.9 p95=36.2
```
Carlos Rivera: interesting — pool=false fixes latency but increases max mem by ~1.8GB?
Alice Nguyen: roughly, yes. Also noticed higher fragmentation counters in the allocator when pool=true.
Bob Chen: fragmentation could cause worse kernel choice due to available contiguous workspace being smaller. v3 probably expects bigger contiguous workspace for its optimized kernels.
Dina Patel: do we have a selector policy that considers available contiguous workspace vs sequence length? right now heuristics choose kernel by model config + seq distribution but not contiguous buffer availability.
Carlos Rivera: we do expose a callback from runtime that queries workspace.free_contiguous_bytes, but it's not used in the default kernel selector. We debated adding it in the RFC but worried about selector complexity.
Alice Nguyen: proposal: update selector to short-circuit to legacy_fused for seq<=threshold when contiguous free < X, where X is kernel-specific workspace_req(seq, dtype). That keeps pool benefits for long seqs but avoids regressions for short.
Bob Chen: sounds reasonable. Two implementation questions: how expensive is workspace.free_contiguous_bytes check (atomic scan)? and should we anneal threshold over time (adaptive)?
Dina Patel: we can sample contiguous availability every N alloc attempts rather than every request. Also store a moving average per-device. That keeps overhead low.
Carlos Rivera: plus we should capture telemetry: when selector falls back because of contiguous shortage, emit metric tag kernel_fallback_reason=workspace_contiguous. That helps correlate with pool size.
Alice Nguyen: agreed. Also saw regressions are worse with mixed-precision quantization enabled (int8/q4). v3 path sometimes chooses an optimized fp16 kernel that triggers extra casts.
Bob Chen: then selector must be dtype-aware too. We already pass dtype, but need to ensure we pick kernels that don't incur extra cast roundtrips for the request dtype.
Dina Patel: could add kernel.cost_estimate(seq, batch, dtype) and pick min(cost) subject to contiguous constraint. Cost estimate can be offline profiled table plus a dynamic latency multiplier from recent telemetry.
Carlos Rivera: one more gotcha: multi-tenant nodes with NVLink topologies — contiguous free bytes differ depending on fragment placement. We should make pool allocation topology-aware (prefer local GPU fragments) and expose locality to selector.
Alice Nguyen: good call. For immediate canary fix I'll disable pool for seq<=64 and emit workspace metrics. Longer term: implement contiguous-aware selector with sampling and telemetry-driven cost model.
Bob Chen: can you open a small follow-up RFC/PR describing selector changes + the telemetry fields? I'll take the allocator topology bits.
Alice Nguyen: will do. Drafting PR now. TL;DR: short-term mitigation = disable pooling for tiny seq, add fallback metric; long-term = contiguous-aware, dtype-sensitive cost selector + topology-aware pooling.
Carlos Rivera: :thumbsup: please include a short test harness that runs seq mix (8/32/512/1024) with pool on/off and quant flags so ops team can reproduce.
infra-bot: Canary deployment 1836001400 started (flash_v3 selector=v1). Check /deployments/1836001400 for logs.
Dina Patel: awesome. I'll watch the canary and collect allocator counters. Thanks Alice.
